records.title: Nobel Prizes 2026 at a glance
records.text: Nobel Prizes 2026 at a glance All six 2026 prizes in one table: who won, when it was announced, and what for. Announced 5 to 12 October 2026 Medicine on 5 October, Physics on 6 October, Chemistry on 7 October, Literature on 8 October, Peace on 9 October, Economic Sciences on 12 October. Medicine: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel, for light-gated ion channels and optogenetics. Physics: Francis Halzen, for IceCube and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. Chemistry: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai, for non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis. Literature: Anne Carson, a Canadian poet and writer. Peace: Navanethem "Navi" Pillay, for her efforts to promote peace and international law. Economic Sciences: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford, for microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation. The physics, chemistry, literature and economics reports give the prize as 12 million Swedish crowns, about $1.2 million.

records.title: Physics: Francis Halzen and the IceCube neutrino detector
records.text: Physics: Francis Halzen and the IceCube neutrino detector One laureate, for helping find very energetic neutrinos that come from cosmic sources. Physics prize announced 6 October 2026 Laureate: Francis Halzen, a Belgian-American particle physicist. Sole laureate. Citation as reported: "for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin". Prize: 12 million Swedish crowns, about $1.2 million (Reuters-carried report).

records.title: Medicine: switching nerve cells on and off with light
records.text: Medicine: switching nerve cells on and off with light Three scientists share the prize for light-gated ion channels, the basis of optogenetics. Medicine prize announced 5 October 2026 Laureates, shared equally: Karl Deisseroth (Stanford University, United States), Peter Hegemann (Humboldt University, Berlin) and Georg Nagel (University of Würzburg, Germany). The work: light-gated ion channels. These are proteins that open when light hits them and let charged particles through. The use: optogenetics. Light switches nerve cells on or off, so a researcher can control single cells. The committee said the method "is now being used in laboratories around the world to reveal the brain's mysteries".

records.title: Chemistry: how mirror-image molecules might end up one-sided
records.text: Chemistry: how mirror-image molecules might end up one-sided Two chemists, for showing how a tiny imbalance can get amplified into a strong one-sided outcome. Chemistry prize announced 7 October 2026 Laureates, shared: Henri B. Kagan (Université Paris-Sud, Orsay, France, aged 95) and Kenso Soai (Tokyo University of Science, aged 76). Citation as quoted: "for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis". Prize: 12 million Swedish crowns, about $1.2 million. Medals are presented in Stockholm on 10 December.

records.title: Literature: Anne Carson and the classical tradition
records.text: Literature: Anne Carson and the classical tradition A Canadian poet and writer. Her work mixes verse, prose, translation and performance. Literature prize announced 8 October 2026 Laureate: Anne Carson, Canadian poet and writer. Born in Toronto. Icelandic citizenship since 2022. Aged 76. Swedish Academy citation: "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature". Prize: 12 million Swedish crowns, about $1.2 million (report).

records.title: Peace: Navi Pillay and the rule of law
records.sub: Peace prize announced 9 October 2026 in Oslo
records.text: Peace: Navi Pillay and the rule of law A former UN human rights chief, honoured for work on peace and international law. Peace prize announced 9 October 2026 in Oslo Laureate: Navanethem "Navi" Pillay, aged 85. The reports say she was born in Durban, South Africa, to a family of Tamil heritage. Committee citation: "efforts to promote peace and international law". The committee also praised her "firm moral compass". Positions: former UN High Commissioner for Human Rights. She has also served as a judge ad hoc at the International Court of Justice in The Gambia v. Myanmar, a case under the Genocide Convention (UN biography). Nominations: 287 candidates this year, 208 individuals and 79 organisations (as reported).

records.title: Economics: Hall and Woodford on steadying the economy
records.text: Economics: Hall and Woodford on steadying the economy Two American economists, for the microeconomic basis of how policy should respond to booms and slumps. Economic Sciences prize announced 12 October 2026 Laureates, shared equally: Robert E. Hall (Stanford University) and Michael Woodford (Columbia University). Both American economists. Royal Swedish Academy citation: "for microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation". Prize: 12 million Swedish crowns, about $1.2 million.

records.title: Fields Medal 2026: four mathematicians at the Philadelphia congress
records.text: Fields Medal 2026: four mathematicians at the Philadelphia congress The top prize in mathematics went to four researchers, announced at the International Congress of Mathematicians. Announced 23 July 2026 Announced at the opening of the International Congress of Mathematicians (ICM), Philadelphia, on 23 July 2026. The congress ran until 30 July. Winners: Yu Deng (University of Chicago), John Pardon (Stony Brook University), Jacob Tsimerman (University of Toronto), Hong Wang (New York University and IHÉS, France). Ages as reported: Deng and Pardon 37, Tsimerman 38, Wang 35. Work areas: Hong Wang, in harmonic analysis and geometric measure theory (IMU citation). Deng in partial differential equations, Pardon in symplectic geometry, Tsimerman in algebraic geometry (as reported).

records.title: Artemis II: the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since 1972
records.text: Artemis II: the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since 1972 Four astronauts flew a crewed lunar flyby and came home safely. It tested the systems for the later landing. Flight in April 2026 Crew: Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen. Launched 1 April 2026. Splashdown was 10 April 2026 (NASA mission page). It was the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972. The lunar flyby used a free-return trajectory. That brings the spacecraft back toward Earth without a major engine burn. NASA still fired smaller burns. The final one lasted 8 seconds and changed Orion's speed by 4.2 feet per second, pushing it toward Earth before splashdown (NASA mission blog). At closest approach the crew was 4,067 miles above the lunar surface. At its farthest, the spacecraft was 252,756 miles from Earth (NASA post-mission account). NASA called it a crewed systems validation test. The data feeds planning for Artemis III, a planned south-pole landing.

records.title: AI Impact Summit 2026: the New Delhi Declaration
records.sub: Summit held in February 2026, New Delhi
records.text: AI Impact Summit 2026: the New Delhi Declaration India hosted a global AI summit in February 2026. The main outcome is a non-binding declaration built on seven pillars. Summit held in February 2026, New Delhi Venue: Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The PIB release gives the summit dates as 18 to 19 February 2026. The declaration was gathered in New Delhi on 19 February. Outcome: the New Delhi Declaration on AI Impact, built on the principle "Welfare for all, Happiness for all". Endorsements: 92 countries and international organisations, according to the PIB release. Earlier news reports gave 88, 89 or 91. Seven pillars: democratising AI resources; economic growth and social good; secure and trusted AI; AI for science; access for social empowerment; human capital development; resilient, efficient and innovative AI systems. Framing: three "Sutras", People, Planet and Progress.

records.title: Union Budget 2026-27: the key numbers
records.text: Union Budget 2026-27: the key numbers Presented on 1 February 2026. The fiscal targets, the big allocations and the new schemes. Presented 1 February 2026 Presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on 1 February 2026. Reports describe the theme as "Yuva Shakti". Total expenditure: about ₹53.47 lakh crore, about 7.7% above the revised estimate for 2025-26 (PRS). Capital expenditure: about ₹12.2 lakh crore. Fiscal deficit target: 4.3% of GDP for FY27, down from 4.4%. Nominal GDP growth assumed at 10%. Health ministry allocation: about ₹1,06,530 crore, nearly 10% above the revised estimate. Income tax slabs unchanged for assessment year 2026-27.

records.title: Padma Awards 2026: 131 honours
records.text: Padma Awards 2026: 131 honours Announced on 25 January 2026, on the eve of Republic Day. The list covers the three civilian tiers and includes posthumous honours. Announced 25 January 2026 Total: 131 awards. Five Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri, per the MHA list. Padma Vibhushan (as reported): Dharmendra Singh Deol and V S Achuthanandan, both posthumously; K T Thomas (public affairs); N Rajam (art); P Narayanan (literature and education). Padma Bhushan (as reported): Alka Yagnik (singer), Mammootty (actor), Uday Kotak (industrialist), Vijay Amritraj (tennis), Bhagat Singh Koshyari, and Piyush Pandey and Shibu Soren, both posthumously. Breakdown reported: 19 women, 16 posthumous awardees and 6 foreigners, NRIs, PIOs or OCI cardholders.

records.title: RBI raises repo rate to 5.50%: the first hike since February 2023
records.text: RBI raises repo rate to 5.50%: the first hike since February 2023 The MPC moved the repo rate up by 25 basis points. The vote on the rate was unanimous; the change of stance was not. Decided 7 October 2026 Repo rate raised by 25 basis points, from 5.25% to 5.50%, under the liquidity adjustment facility (LAF). The MPC voted unanimously on the rate. Standing deposit facility (SDF) rate: 5.25%. Marginal standing facility (MSF) rate, also the Bank Rate: 5.75% (RBI release). The MPC also changed the stance from neutral to "calibrated tightening". Two members, Dr Nagesh Kumar and Prof Ram Singh, wanted the stance to stay neutral (RBI release). Projections: real GDP growth for 2026-27 at 7.1%; CPI inflation for 2026-27 at 5.2% (RBI release). The 63rd MPC meeting ran from 5 to 7 October 2026. The next meeting is scheduled for 2 to 4 December 2026 (RBI release).

records.title: Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Act, 2026
records.text: Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Act, 2026 Parliament passed the amendment in the Monsoon Session and the President gave assent on 31 July 2026. It covers UPSC, so every aspirant should know what it does. Act No. 10 of 2026, assent 31 July 2026 Act No. 10 of 2026, assented to on 31 July 2026. It amends the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 (Gazette text, as transcribed by a non-government site; the e-Gazette PDF was not reachable from the build environment). The Act amends section 12 so that investigation can be handed to a Special Task Force that the Central Government constitutes by notification. Where a Special Task Force is constituted, only it investigates. Investigations must be completed within two months, counted from the date of the information (or the reference or notification to the Central Investigating Agency or the Special Task Force). Each State Government and Union Territory Administration, after consulting the Chief Justice of the High Court, designates a Court of Session as a Special Fast Track Court, by notification. Trials proceed day-to-day, and Special Public Prosecutors are appointed for these courts. Trials must be completed within three months of the chargesheet being filed, or, for an already-pending transferred case, of its receipt by the designated court. Appeals lie to the High Court against a judgment, sentence or order of these courts that is not interlocutory, and are heard by a bench of two High Court judges. The High Court may also hear separate appeals against orders granting or refusing bail. An appeal is filed within thirty days of the judgment, sentence or order appealed against, which the High Court may extend for sufficient cause, but no appeal is entertained after ninety days. The appeal is to be disposed of within three months of its admission, as far as possible. The penalties are revised. The figures in the bill as introduced are in the PRS summary. Check the enacted sections 10 to 12 for the final numbers.

records.title: Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2026
records.sub: Act No. 14 of 2026, assent 11 August 2026, deemed in force from 16 May 2026
records.text: Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2026 Raises the maximum number of Supreme Court judges, other than the Chief Justice, from 33 to 37. It replaces the ordinance of 16 May 2026, and it was deemed in force from that date. Act No. 14 of 2026, assent 11 August 2026, deemed in force from 16 May 2026 Act No. 14 of 2026, assented to on 11 August 2026. Deemed to have come into force on 16 May 2026 (Gazette text, as transcribed by a non-government site). Amends section 2 of the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956, replacing "thirty-three" with "thirty-seven". The maximum number of Supreme Court judges, other than the Chief Justice, goes from 33 to 37. Repeals the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026. Anything done under the ordinance is treated as done under the 1956 Act as amended. Introduced in Lok Sabha on 20 July 2026 (PRS). PIB's Monsoon Session summary says both Houses passed it (PIB, 13 August 2026).

records.title: Tribunals Reforms Act, 2026: the National Tribunals Commission
records.sub: Act No. 17 of 2026, assent 13 August 2026; all provisions in force 25 August 2026
records.text: Tribunals Reforms Act, 2026: the National Tribunals Commission Assent on 13 August 2026. It repeals the 2021 tribunals law. The Act provides for a National Tribunals Commission; its establishment date is to be appointed by a separate notification. Act No. 17 of 2026, assent 13 August 2026; all provisions in force 25 August 2026 Act No. 17 of 2026, assented to on 13 August 2026 (Gazette text, as transcribed by a non-government site). All provisions came into force on 25 August 2026 under notification S.O. 4713(E) of the same date. Section 3 provides that the National Tribunals Commission is established from a date that the Central Government appoints by notification in the Official Gazette. The notices read here do not give that establishment date. Chairperson: a person who is or has been a Supreme Court judge or a Chief Justice of a High Court. Judicial members: a person who is or has been a Chief Justice or judge of a High Court. Technical members: at least 25 years of special knowledge and experience in public administration, finance, law, accountancy, banking, management or technology. Functions include selection for tribunal vacancies, review of tribunal performance, inquiry into complaints about members' conduct, and a National Tribunals Data Grid (bill as introduced, PRS).

records.title: Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026: state levies on mineral rights
records.sub: Act No. 20 of 2026, assent 17 August 2026; in force 22 August 2026 (per the ZC-03 review)
records.text: Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026: state levies on mineral rights Assent on 17 August 2026. It limits state levies on mineral rights and mineral-bearing land, with a new section 9D. It raises a federalism question and an equality question. Act No. 20 of 2026, assent 17 August 2026; in force 22 August 2026 (per the ZC-03 review) Act No. 20 of 2026, assented to on 17 August 2026 (Gazette text, as transcribed by a non-government site). Inserts section 9D. A State levy on mineral rights or mineral-bearing land, whether based on quantity, value or royalty, is allowed only under conditions the Central Government prescribes. Section 9D deems invalid any such levy that had not been deposited with the State Government or recovered by it before the Act's commencement. Amounts already deposited or recovered are not refundable. Section 13(2) is amended to cover the conditions or restrictions on levies under section 9D. A new definition of "mineral bearing land" is added to section 3. Commencement: the Central Government appointed the date of publication of S.O. 4642(E), 22 August 2026, as the effective date. The transcription was checked; the official PDF was not reached.

records.title: INS Samarthak: the first multi-purpose vessel, built by a private yard
records.text: INS Samarthak: the first multi-purpose vessel, built by a private yard Commissioned on 16 October 2026. First of its class, and the first major warship built by an Indian private shipyard. Commissioned 16 October 2026 First of class of Multi-Purpose Vessels (MPVs) for the Indian Navy. Designed and built by L&T Shipyard, the first major warship built by an Indian private shipyard (PIB). Over 75% indigenous content, with modular construction and pre-outfitting (PIB). Presided over by Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan. Chief of the Naval Staff: Admiral Krishna Swaminathan. Conceived as a versatile platform for trials and evaluation.

records.title: CAQM extends PTZ camera monitoring to all NCR industries under Direction 98
records.text: CAQM extends PTZ camera monitoring to all NCR industries under Direction 98 A new order makes remote camera monitoring of fuel use and emissions mandatory for a wider set of NCR industries, with a 30 November 2026 deadline. Order reported 16 October 2026 Commission: Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM). The order extends the PTZ (pan-tilt-zoom) camera requirement to all industries covered under Statutory Direction No. 98. Covered: all 17 highly polluting categories identified by CPCB, Red Category (medium and large) air-polluting industries, food and food processing and textile units with boilers or thermic fluid heaters, and metal industries with furnaces. Deadline: the order says the installation and operation of the required PTZ cameras, with real-time transmission of video feeds, must be done by 30 November 2026 (PIB release quoting the order). The order supersedes an earlier CAQM order of 5 October 2026.

records.title: PMAY-Urban 2.0: 1.93 lakh more houses approved at one CSMC meeting
records.text: PMAY-Urban 2.0: 1.93 lakh more houses approved at one CSMC meeting The 10th CSMC meeting approved more houses. Cumulative sanctions under the mission now stand at 20.80 lakh. CSMC meeting held 16 October 2026 Scheme: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0), run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA). Meeting: 10th Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC), 16 October 2026, chaired by the Secretary, Department of Urban Development. Approved at this meeting: 1.93 lakh additional houses. Cumulative sanctions under the mission: 20.80 lakh. At this meeting, the approvals were for EWS families under the Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC) and Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) verticals. Largest approvals in this round: Uttar Pradesh (73,182), Bihar (52,866), Telangana (18,120) and West Bengal (16,559).

records.title: Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026: no further action after the Lok Sabha motion
records.sub: Introduced 16 April 2026; motion failed in April 2026 (PIB)
records.text: Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026: no further action after the Lok Sabha motion The bill to expand the Lok Sabha and change the basis of delimitation did not get the two-thirds majority it needed. PIB says no further action was taken. Introduced 16 April 2026; motion failed in April 2026 (PIB) Introduced in Lok Sabha on 16 April 2026, together with the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 and the Delimitation Bill, 2026 (PRS). PIB, Budget Session 2026 summary (18 April 2026): the bill "could not have the required majority as per Article 368(2)" on its motion for consideration, so "no further action was taken". The two dependent bills were "not proceeded further". Vote tally, from news reports only (LiveLaw, Vision IAS): 298 members for and 230 against, out of 528 present and voting, short of the two-thirds required. The official division record was not reached. As introduced, the constitutional bill raised the maximum size of the Lok Sabha to 850 members: up to 815 from the States and up to 35 from the Union Territories (PRS). PRS says the bills remove the fixed census provision. The Delimitation Bill, 2026 would use the latest published census, which PRS says implies the 2011 census for the next delimitation.

records.title: Sukhna Wetland and Sauj Jheel join the Ramsar List
records.text: Sukhna Wetland and Sauj Jheel join the Ramsar List A 15 October announcement adds two very different wetlands: an urban-edge reservoir and a Ganga floodplain lake. Designation announced 15 October 2026 The Convention on Wetlands announced Sukhna Wetland and Sauj Jheel as new Ramsar sites on 15 October. Its release and the Environment Ministry put India’s announced total at 103. Sukhna Wetland (site 2602) lies beside Chandigarh at the foot of the Outer Himalayas. It is a peri-urban reservoir whose catchment affects water and sediment flows. Sauj Jheel (site 2603) is a shallow lake in Uttar Pradesh’s Ganga floodplain, near Saman Bird Sanctuary. The Convention describes it as a habitat for waterbirds and reports more than 30,000 birds there regularly. The Convention on Wetlands was adopted at Ramsar, Iran, in 1971 and entered into force in 1975. It entered into force for India on 1 February 1982.

records.title: PLFS September 2026: read the basis with the rate
records.text: PLFS September 2026: read the basis with the rate The monthly bulletin puts unemployment at 5.0% for people aged 15 and above under Current Weekly Status. The denominator and survey window belong beside the figure. Bulletin released 15 October 2026 The National Statistical Office under MoSPI conducts the Periodic Labour Force Survey. The September bulletin reports all-India monthly indicators for people aged 15 and above using Current Weekly Status (CWS). For September, the bulletin reports LFPR at 55.5%, WPR at 52.7% and unemployment at 5.0%. Each figure uses the CWS basis. Urban LFPR rose from 50.4% in August to 50.7% in September; the all-India LFPR remained close to 55.5%. The bulletin also reports a 6.9% urban unemployment rate for September. MoSPI revised the PLFS sampling design from January 2025 to support more frequent estimates. Its published comparison note says this can affect comparability with earlier estimates.

records.title: Cabinet approves NSAP continuation; release sets three-month guideline window
records.text: Cabinet approves NSAP continuation; release sets three-month guideline window The Cabinet approved continuation through 2030–31 and higher disability assistance. Its release says revised guidelines will be issued and implemented within three months; current operational status was not independently checked. Cabinet approval announced 14 October 2026 The Union Cabinet approved ₹53,428 crore to continue the National Social Assistance Programme from 2026–27 to 2030–31. The release says the approval covers 3.20 crore beneficiaries across all 36 States and Union Territories. The programme is to be called Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana. The approved component names include Pradhan Mantri Vridhavastha Pension Yojana (old age), Pradhan Mantri Vidhawa Pension Yojana (widow), Pradhan Mantri Divyangjan Pension Yojana (disability) and Pradhan Mantri Parivar Labh Yojana (family benefit). For disability pension, the approved assistance is ₹375 for ages 0–79 and ₹625 from age 80. The benchmark-disability threshold changes from 80% to 40%, and the minimum-age rule changes to cover people from birth. The Cabinet release says guidelines setting the revised eligibility, coverage and assistance are to be issued and implemented within three months. Article 41 of the Constitution is the public-assistance directive. It asks the State to act within its economic capacity and development.

records.title: Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill defeated
records.text: Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill defeated Polity The Bill won 298 votes against 230 with 528 members present and voting, short of the two-thirds (352) needed. It would have expanded the Lok Sabha to about 850 seats, delimited seats on the 2011 Census, and linked this to women's reservation. The companion Delimitation Bill and UT Laws Bill were withdrawn. Article 368 special majority. Articles 81 and 82: the freeze on seats was set by the 42nd Amendment (1971 Census) and extended by the 84th Amendment to the first Census after 2026. Article 334A (106th Amendment, 2023). Delimitation Act, 2002. PRS Budget Session 2026 wrap; PIB, 18 Apr 2026

records.title: Kerala renamed Keralam
records.sub: Polity Assent Aug 2026; in force 25 Aug 2026
records.text: Kerala renamed Keralam Polity Parliament passed the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 after the President referred it to the Kerala Assembly for its views, which the Assembly gave unanimously in July. Article 3 procedure: President's recommendation, referral to the State legislature (its views are not binding), simple majority, not an amendment under Article 368. Earlier renames: Orissa to Odisha (2011), Uttaranchal to Uttarakhand (2007). Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026; MHA notification of 25 Aug 2026

records.title: VB-G RAM G Act replaces MGNREGA
records.text: VB-G RAM G Act replaces MGNREGA Polity The Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025 raises the rural work guarantee from 100 to 125 days, lets States notify an agricultural pause of up to 60 days a year, and moves to a 60:40 Centre-State funding pattern. Statute versus scheme. Article 41 (Directive Principle on the right to work). Unemployment allowance and delayed-payment compensation. Panchayats' role. PIB, 21 Dec 2025 (assent) and 30 Jun 2026 (commencement)

records.title: Census 2027 under way
records.text: Census 2027 under way Polity Houselisting ran through 2026 ahead of population enumeration, with caste enumeration included for the first time since 1931. Reference date 1 March 2027, and 1 October 2026 for snow-bound areas. Census Act, 1948. Census is in the Union List. Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Home Ministry. Link to delimitation under Article 82. PIB Census 2027 backgrounder (Apr 2026); Lok Sabha reply, Dec 2025

records.title: Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment
records.text: Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Polity Parliament passed a Bill replacing an ordinance to raise the Supreme Court's sanctioned strength. Article 124(1): Parliament fixes the number of judges by law. Article 123: an ordinance lapses six weeks after Parliament reassembles unless approved. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: Anti-paper-leak law strengthened
records.text: Anti-paper-leak law strengthened Polity The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill provides time-bound investigation and trial and Special Fast Track Courts. A high-powered task force under Nandan Nilekani is working on examination reform. Public Examinations Act, 2024. Fast Track Courts. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: Other Monsoon Session laws
records.text: Other Monsoon Session laws Polity The Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 2026 replaces the 1891 law to recognise digital banking records. Also passed: Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment), Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment), MSMED (Amendment) and MMDR (Amendment). The FCRA Amendment went to a Joint Committee; the ISI Bill is pending. Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. Joint Parliamentary Committees. Bill stages. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: New Income Tax Act in force
records.text: New Income Tax Act in force Polity The Income Tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act, introducing a single 'tax year' in place of 'previous year' and 'assessment year'. Money Bill versus Finance Bill. Article 265: no tax without authority of law. PIB, 1 Apr 2026 (Act passed 12 Aug 2025, assent 21 Aug 2025, Rules 20 Mar 2026)

records.title: GDP, CPI and IIP rebased
records.text: GDP, CPI and IIP rebased Economy GDP was rebased to 2022-23 (released 27 Feb 2026), CPI to 2024=100 (12 Feb 2026) and IIP to 2022-23 (May 2026). Manufacturing now uses double deflation, and GST, e-Vahan and PFMS data feed the estimates. The advisory committee (ACNAS) was chaired by Biswanath Goldar. Base year concept. The RBI targets CPI (Combined) inflation. Single versus double deflation. MoSPI and NSO. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: Union Budget 2026-27
records.text: Union Budget 2026-27 Economy Fiscal deficit target 4.3% of GDP; capex Rs 12.2 lakh crore (3.1% of GDP). New: India Semiconductor Mission 2.0, Electronics Components scheme raised to Rs 40,000 crore, Biopharma SHAKTI (Rs 10,000 crore), rare-earth corridors in Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, Bharat-VISTAAR (AI farm advisory on AgriStack), TReDS mandatory for central government purchases, a Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund, the Dankuni-Surat freight corridor, a Khelo India Mission, and NIMHANS-2 with upgrades at Ranchi and Tezpur. Fiscal deficit definition. TReDS (asked in 2026 via M1xchange). Rare earths (asked in 2026). Article 112 Annual Financial Statement. Budget Speech 2026-27, 1 Feb 2026 (indiabudget.gov.in)

records.title: India-EU free trade agreement concluded
records.text: India-EU free trade agreement concluded Economy Talks that began in 2007 were concluded, with deep tariff cuts on Indian exports. Signing follows legal review, and entry into force is expected around early 2027. The India-UK CETA came into force in July 2026; deals with Oman and New Zealand were also finalised. The EU is a customs union of 27 members (EU membership was asked in 2026). FTA versus CEPA versus CETA. The EU's carbon border tax (CBAM). Ministry of Commerce, 27 Jan 2026; European Commission status page (Sep 2026)

records.title: Oil shock from the Iran war
records.text: Oil shock from the Iran war Economy After US and Israeli strikes on Iran, Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz closed in early March 2026. Brent crude passed $120 and India faced LPG shortages. A June arrangement briefly reopened the Strait before it broke down; in August Iran and Oman agreed to reopen it for 60 days. Strategic petroleum reserves (ISPRL caverns at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur). Alternative routes: INSTC, Chabahar, IMEC. Bab-el-Mandeb and the Houthis. Map: Musandam, Gulf of Oman versus Persian Gulf coasts. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: Make in India at 12
records.text: Make in India at 12 Economy Electronics production rose from about Rs 1.9 lakh crore (2014-15) to Rs 13.11 lakh crore (2025-26). Make in India 2.0 covers 27 sectors. PLI schemes cover 14 sectors. Executive initiative versus statute. PLI design. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: August 2026 Cabinet approvals
records.text: August 2026 Cabinet approvals Economy Reported: a 'Samudra Manthan' offshore exploration scheme (Rs 84,084 crore), an extension of PM-KISAN, and a larger Khelo India. The Independence Day speech restated the target of 100 GW of nuclear power by 2047. Offshore hydrocarbon exploration; PM-KISAN as a central sector scheme; the nuclear three-stage programme. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: India holds the BRICS chair
records.text: India holds the BRICS chair IR India chaired BRICS in 2026. The 18th Summit met in New Delhi (Bharat Mandapam) on 12-13 Sep 2026 under the theme 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability' and adopted the New Delhi Declaration. BRICS membership after expansion; New Development Bank (Shanghai); Contingent Reserve Arrangement. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: First direct India-Nepal container freight train
records.text: First direct India-Nepal container freight train IR A train ran directly from Kolkata Port to Biratnagar under the revised India-Nepal Rail Transit Protocol, with no transhipment at the border. Cross-border connectivity (2026 asked about river bridges with neighbours). Nepal is landlocked; transit treaty. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: Defence hardware made in India
records.text: Defence hardware made in India IR INS Mahendragiri, the sixth Project 17A stealth frigate, was commissioned. INS Nipun, the second Nistar-class diving support vessel, was built by Hindustan Shipyard. 'Sher' AK-203 rifles are now made at Korwa, Amethi, by the Indo-Russian joint venture. 2026 asked which defence items are made in India. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: Nauru renamed Republic of Naoero
records.text: Nauru renamed Republic of Naoero IR The Pacific island state, the world's third-smallest country by area (after Vatican City and Monaco), changed its name and its country code to NRO. Pacific geography; microstates. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: New Chief of Defence Staff
records.text: New Chief of Defence Staff IR General N. S. Raja Subramani became Chief of Defence Staff and Secretary, Department of Military Affairs, succeeding General Anil Chauhan. CDS heads the Department of Military Affairs. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: Glaw Lake: Arunachal's first Ramsar site
records.text: Glaw Lake: Arunachal's first Ramsar site Environment India's 101st Ramsar site, a freshwater lake in the Eastern Himalayas inside the Kamlang Tiger Reserve. Ramsar Convention (1971, Iran). Montreux Record. Ramsar sites by State. Your North-East edge. Ramsar Convention site notice, Aug 2026

records.title: COP30 Belém outcomes and COP31
records.text: COP30 Belém outcomes and COP31 Environment COP30 launched the Tropical Forests Forever Facility, a payment-for-results fund targeting about US$125 billion, with at least 20% for Indigenous peoples and local communities, plus the Belém Health Action Plan and a tripling of adaptation finance. COP31 is in Antalya, 9 to 20 November 2026, with Türkiye hosting and Australia leading negotiations. UNFCCC, Paris Agreement, NDCs, REDD+ (asked in 2026), adaptation versus mitigation finance. UNFCCC session records (COP30, 10-22 Nov 2025); COP30 Executive Report, 19 Mar 2026; unfccc.int/cop31

records.title: UNCCD COP17 and India's grassland guide
records.text: UNCCD COP17 and India's grassland guide Environment At UNCCD COP17 in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, India launched its first guide to grasslands and other open natural ecosystems. UNCCD (desertification). Land degradation neutrality. Open natural ecosystems misclassified as 'wastelands'. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: Mizoram museum named a biodiversity repository
records.text: Mizoram museum named a biodiversity repository Environment Mizoram University's Natural History Museum became India's 21st Designated Repository under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002. Biological Diversity Act 2002 and its 2023 amendment. National Biodiversity Authority. Indo-Burma hotspot. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: Access and Benefit-Sharing payout
records.text: Access and Benefit-Sharing payout Environment The National Biodiversity Authority disbursed about Rs 2.82 crore, most of it through 27 State Biodiversity Boards. Nagoya Protocol. NBA (Chennai). State Biodiversity Boards and Biodiversity Management Committees. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: India's first soil texture map
records.text: India's first soil texture map Environment Built by the National Bureau of Soil Survey and Land Use Planning from satellite and remote-sensing data, at hectare level. Soil types and texture classes (NCERT). Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: Sarnath becomes India's 45th World Heritage Site
records.text: Sarnath becomes India's 45th World Heritage Site History Inscribed at the 48th World Heritage Committee session in Busan, South Korea. India's 44th was the Maratha Military Landscapes (2025). Buddha's first sermon (dharmachakra-pravartana). Ashoka's lion capital (the national emblem). Dhamek and Chaukhandi stupas. 2026 asked what an empty seat symbolises. UNESCO, 48th session of the World Heritage Committee, Busan, 25 Jul 2026

records.title: Vande Mataram at 150
records.text: Vande Mataram at 150 History Year-long commemoration; the 2026 Independence Day theme highlighted it, and a 2026 amendment brings the song under the national-honour law. Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, Anandamath (1882). Adopted as the national song on 24 January 1950 with equal honour to the anthem. Swadeshi movement. PIB backgrounder, 6 Nov 2025 (year-long commemoration from 7 Nov 2025)

records.title: Sardar Patel's 150th birth anniversary
records.text: Sardar Patel's 150th birth anniversary History Commemoration year for Vallabhbhai Patel (born 31 October 1875). Kheda (1918), Bardoli (1928, asked in 2026), integration of princely States, Statue of Unity. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: Birsa Munda's 150th birth anniversary
records.text: Birsa Munda's 150th birth anniversary History Observed as Janjatiya Gaurav Varsh. Ulgulan (1899-1900), Chotanagpur Tenancy Act 1908, Munda and Santhal uprisings. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: Gaganyaan G1 uncrewed flight
records.text: Gaganyaan G1 uncrewed flight S&T The first uncrewed orbital test, carrying the half-humanoid robot Vyommitra on the human-rated LVM3. Crewed flight targeted for 2027; first Bharatiya Antariksh Station module by 2028 and the station by 2035. Crew escape system, re-entry and recovery, human-rating. PIB, 6 Aug 2026 (first uncrewed mission with Vyommitra targeted for Q4 2026)

records.title: Launch year for ISRO and private players
records.text: Launch year for ISRO and private players S&T GSLV-F17 placed EOS-05 in orbit in September 2026, with NVS-03 (NavIC) next. The first industry-built PSLV (HAL and L&T) and Skyroot's Vikram-1 are in the pipeline. NavIC, GSLV versus PSLV, IN-SPACe and private launches (asked in 2026). Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: Deepak Dhar wins the Dirac Medal
records.text: Deepak Dhar wins the Dirac Medal S&T Awarded by the ICTP (Italy) for work in statistical physics, especially the Abelian sandpile model, shared with Derrida, Mézard and Sompolinsky. Indian scientists in global awards; 2026 asked a Nobel laureate. Zola Corpus v1 (26 Sep 2026); not re-checked in the Oct 2026 round

records.title: Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill with a Joint Committee
records.sub: Polity Introduced 20 Aug 2025; JPC report due Winter Session 2026
records.text: Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill with a Joint Committee Polity The Bill provides for removing a Prime Minister, Chief Minister or minister who stays in custody for 30 consecutive days on charges carrying five or more years of imprisonment. It was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee, which deferred adopting its report on 17 Jul 2026; its deadline now runs to the Winter Session 2026. Articles 75, 164 and 239AA (appointment and tenure of ministers). Article 368 special majority. Joint committees versus departmentally related standing committees. PRS Bill Track and committee record

records.title: Supreme Court opinion on Governors' assent to Bills
records.text: Supreme Court opinion on Governors' assent to Bills Polity Answering Special Reference No. 1 of 2025 under Article 143, the Supreme Court gave an advisory opinion on how Governors and the President handle State Bills: assent, withholding assent, and reservation for the President. Article 200 (Governor's options), Article 201 (Bills reserved for the President), Article 143 (advisory jurisdiction; the opinion is advisory, not a binding decree). Supreme Court of India, judgment of 20 Nov 2025

records.title: Supreme Court on AI-fabricated citations
records.text: Supreme Court on AI-fabricated citations Polity In Pooja Ramesh Singh v J&K Bank (2026 INSC 668), the Supreme Court set aside NCLT and NCLAT orders because the NCLT had relied on fictitious, apparently AI-generated precedents. It declared zero tolerance: citing unverified AI case law is professional misconduct, and relying on it is a serious judicial lapse. Precedent and Article 141. Duties of advocates. AI governance in courts. Supreme Court of India, judgment summary, 2 Jul 2026

records.title: CJI Surya Kant takes office
records.text: CJI Surya Kant takes office Polity Justice Surya Kant became Chief Justice of India with effect from 24 Nov 2025; the appointment was notified on 30 Oct 2025. Article 124(2) appointment by the President; the seniority convention; the collegium; Memorandum of Procedure. PIB, 30 Oct 2025

records.title: DPDP Rules notified, phased commencement
records.text: DPDP Rules notified, phased commencement Polity The Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 were notified on 13 Nov 2025. Commencement is phased, and the 18-month tranche falls in May 2027, the month of the Prelims. Right to privacy under Article 21 (Puttaswamy, 2017). Data Protection Board. Data fiduciary versus data principal. Delegated legislation. PIB press note, 17 Nov 2025; Gazette notification, 13 Nov 2025

records.title: Online gaming law and Rules in force
records.sub: Polity Act Aug 2025; Rules from 1 May 2026
records.text: Online gaming law and Rules in force Polity The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 separates e-sports and social games from online money games. Rules announced on 22 Apr 2026 took effect on 1 May 2026. Union power over the subject; regulatory authority design; Act versus Rules. Gazette, 22 Aug 2025; PIB, 22 Apr 2026

records.title: Four Labour Codes in force
records.text: Four Labour Codes in force Economy The four Labour Codes took effect on 21 Nov 2025, consolidating 29 central labour laws. Labour is in the Concurrent List. The four codes: Wages; Industrial Relations; Social Security; Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions. Gig and platform workers in the Social Security Code. PIB year-end review, 30 Dec 2025

records.title: GST rates rationalised
records.text: GST rates rationalised Economy The 56th GST Council meeting recommended a simpler structure with two main rates, 5% and 18%, plus a 40% special rate, effective 22 Sep 2025. Article 279A (GST Council: composition, voting weights of Centre and States). Article 246A. Compensation cess. PIB, 8 Sep 2025

records.title: PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana approved
records.text: PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana approved Economy The Cabinet approved the scheme for six years from 2025-26, covering 100 districts with low agricultural productivity. Aspirational-district model; convergence of existing schemes; agriculture as a State subject. PIB, 16 Jul 2025

records.title: PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (employment-linked incentive)
records.text: PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (employment-linked incentive) Economy The Employment Linked Incentive scheme was approved on 1 Jul 2025 and described by PIB in Aug 2025 as the PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana. EPFO registration as the eligibility test; incentives split between first-time employees and employers. PIB, 21 Aug 2025

records.title: Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses
records.text: Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses Economy Approved for 2025-26 to 2030-31 with an announced outlay of Rs 11,440 crore to raise domestic pulses production and cut import dependence. MSP and procurement through NAFED and NCCF; buffer stocks; crop diversification. PIB, 17 Mar 2026

records.title: India-UK CETA enters into force
records.text: India-UK CETA enters into force Economy The Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, signed on 24 Jul 2025, entered into force on 15 Jul 2026 with the Double Contributions Convention on social security. UK tariffs on about 99% of Indian tariff lines went to zero. Signing versus entry into force. FTA versus CEPA versus CETA. Social-security totalisation agreements. Business Wales (UK government), Jul 2026; Ministry of Commerce, 17 Jun 2026

records.title: India-New Zealand FTA signed
records.text: India-New Zealand FTA signed Economy India and New Zealand signed a free trade agreement in New Delhi on 27 Apr 2026. Entry into force had not been confirmed in the sources checked. Stages of a trade agreement; dairy and agriculture sensitivities. Ministry of Commerce, 27 Apr 2026

records.title: WTO MC14 and the fisheries subsidies agreement
records.text: WTO MC14 and the fisheries subsidies agreement IR The WTO's 14th Ministerial Conference met in Yaoundé, Cameroon. The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies had entered into force on 15 Sep 2025. WTO structure (Ministerial Conference, General Council, Dispute Settlement Body). Illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing subsidies. WTO MC14 page and closing release, 30 Mar 2026

records.title: High Seas Treaty (BBNJ) in force
records.text: High Seas Treaty (BBNJ) in force Environment The Agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction entered into force on 17 Jan 2026, 120 days after the 60th ratification. UNCLOS zones (territorial sea, EEZ, high seas). Marine protected areas on the high seas; marine genetic resources. UN Treaty Collection

records.title: New Ramsar sites, Sep 2025 to Jan 2026
records.text: New Ramsar sites, Sep 2025 to Jan 2026 Environment Ramsar notices added Gokul Jalashay and Udaipur Jheel (Sep 2025), Gogabil Lake (Nov 2025), and Chhari Dhand and Patna Bird Sanctuary (Jan 2026). Ramsar Convention (1971, Iran); Montreux Record; criteria for designation; Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules. Ramsar Convention site notices

records.title: G20 Johannesburg summit
records.text: G20 Johannesburg summit IR The first G20 Leaders' Summit on the African continent named solidarity, equality and sustainability as its pillars. G20 troika; the African Union as a permanent member since 2023; G20 has no secretariat. G20 Leaders' Declaration, Johannesburg

records.title: BRICS Rio and SCO Tianjin summits
records.text: BRICS Rio and SCO Tianjin summits IR India attended the BRICS summit in Rio de Janeiro and the 25th SCO summit in Tianjin. BRICS expansion; SCO members and the Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure; map of host cities. MEA summit records

records.title: Global MPI 2025 links poverty to climate hazards
records.text: Global MPI 2025 links poverty to climate hazards Economy UNDP and OPHI's 2025 Global Multidimensional Poverty Index overlaid poverty with climate hazards, with estimates for 109 countries. MPI dimensions (health, education, living standards) and the NITI Aayog national MPI. UNDP, 17 Oct 2025

records.title: Global Innovation Index 2026
records.text: Global Innovation Index 2026 S&T WIPO released GII 2026. India ranked 38th of 139 economies overall (25th on innovation outputs, 49th on inputs) and was an innovation 'overperformer' for the 16th year. WIPO; input versus output sub-indices. WIPO, 29 Sep 2026

records.title: NISAR launched
records.text: NISAR launched S&T The joint NASA-ISRO synthetic aperture radar satellite was launched from Sriharikota. L-band and S-band radar; all-weather, day-night imaging; Sun-synchronous orbit; GSLV. ISRO, 21 Jul 2025

records.title: SHANTI Act opens nuclear energy
records.text: SHANTI Act opens nuclear energy S&T The Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India Act, 2025 received assent on 20 Dec 2025. Atomic Energy Act, 1962; Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010; the AERB. eGazette, 20 Dec 2025

records.title: India AI Impact Summit, New Delhi
records.text: India AI Impact Summit, New Delhi S&T India hosted the AI Impact Summit; the New Delhi Declaration came out of the 18-19 Feb sessions. Summit lineage: Bletchley Park, Seoul, Paris, New Delhi. IndiaAI Mission. PIB declaration; MEA summit record

records.title: Shubhanshu Shukla returns from Axiom-4
records.text: Shubhanshu Shukla returns from Axiom-4 S&T Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla returned from the Axiom-4 mission to the International Space Station. ISS partners; Gaganyaan crew training; microgravity research. NASA, 15 Jul 2025

records.title: Maratha Military Landscapes on the World Heritage List
records.text: Maratha Military Landscapes on the World Heritage List History Twelve forts were inscribed as the Maratha Military Landscapes of India, India's 44th World Heritage property. Fort architecture (hill, coastal, island forts); Shivaji's administration; Gingee in Tamil Nadu. UNESCO World Heritage Committee, 11 Jul 2025

records.title: From Bill to Act: the Union route chooser
records.text: From Bill to Act: the Union route chooser Show that the three kinds of Union Bill (ordinary, Money, Constitution amendment) take genuinely different routes after the first House, and that assent has its own rules.

records.title: A State Bill at the Governor's desk (Arts 200-201 and the 2025 rulings)
records.text: A State Bill at the Governor's desk (Arts 200-201 and the 2025 rulings) Show which options the Governor has at each stage and how the law moved across 2025, including the arrows that are forbidden.

records.title: The Union ordinance stopwatch (Art 123)
records.text: The Union ordinance stopwatch (Art 123) Teach when an ordinance can be made, how long it lives, and what ends it.

records.title: The State ordinance, with the President in the background (Art 213)
records.text: The State ordinance, with the President in the background (Art 213) Teach what differs from the Union ordinance: when the Governor needs the President's instructions, and the bicameral wrinkles.

records.title: Amending the Constitution: the two tests and the half-the-States rule (Art 368)
records.text: Amending the Constitution: the two tests and the half-the-States rule (Art 368) Make the double majority and the ratification rule computable, using the 131st Amendment's defeat as a worked example.

records.title: National emergency: Cabinet, two Houses and two rights routes (Article 352)
records.text: National emergency: Cabinet, two Houses and two rights routes (Article 352) Trace written Cabinet authorization, proclamation, approval, continuance, disapproval and separate rights effects; prevent transplantation of another emergency’s rules.

records.title: President’s Rule: textual gates and Bommai review (Article 356)
records.text: President’s Rule: textual gates and Bommai review (Article 356) Separate constitutional breakdown from political preference, initial approval from continuance, and proclamation review from review of later actions.

records.title: Financial emergency: approval and directions without a renewal clock (Article 360)
records.text: Financial emergency: approval and directions without a renewal clock (Article 360) Separate the constitutional threat test, two-House approval and optional directions; locate State-bill reservation and judges’ salaries without importing Article 356 powers.

records.title: Anti-defection: membership, direction, merger and the adjudicator
records.text: Anti-defection: membership, direction, merger and the adjudicator Distinguish the paragraph2grounds, current defences, proper decision-maker and source-specific timing/review limits without adjudicating contested real facts.

records.title: Centre-State competence, conflict and the assent exception
records.text: Centre-State competence, conflict and the assent exception Establish legislative actor/subject/territory authority before choosing repugnancy, special-law precedence or GST analysis.

records.title: President in a hung Lok Sabha: claims, appointment and confidence
records.text: President in a hung Lok Sabha: claims, appointment and confidence Audit claimed support without manufacturing a binding invitation order; distinguish appointment, ministerial continuity, Lok Sabha confidence and dissolution/advice.

records.title: Governor in a hung Assembly: formation, material and floor confidence
records.text: Governor in a hung Assembly: formation, material and floor confidence Separate initial formation from incumbent confidence, judicially limited discretion from text finality, and actual floor arithmetic from emergency/report/remedy events.

records.title: GST Council: quorum, government weights and recommendation effect
records.text: GST Council: quorum, government weights and recommendation effect Run exact weighted division without confusing members with government voting blocks or a recommendation with operative tax law.

records.title: Money multiplier: observed identity and conditional model
records.text: Money multiplier: observed identity and conditional model Classify RBI monetary stocks and compare a measured money/base ratio with an explicitly assumed C+D teaching model.

records.title: MPC: statutory voting, target provenance and accountability
records.text: MPC: statutory voting, target provenance and accountability Distinguish Government target-setting from MPC policy-rate votes; keep reported target/failure instruments and multiple publication clocks visible.

records.title: MSP to procurement to PDS: price, stock, entitlement and remedy
records.text: MSP to procurement to PDS: price, stock, entitlement and remedy Keep announced farmer price/purchase policy, central pool allocation, identified household grain quantity and short-supply/quality remedies distinct.

records.title: Finance Commission: recommendation, net pool, State share and release
records.text: Finance Commission: recommendation, net pool, State share and release Trace constitutional and statutory authority through documentary responses, exact vertical/horizontal arithmetic and separate grant conditions.

records.title: Article 311: authority, inquiry and exceptional routes
records.text: Article 311: authority, inquiry and exceptional routes Separate a disciplinary allegation from competent authority, fair inquiry and a specifically justified constitutional exception.

records.title: CAG to PAC: report, scrutiny and action taken
records.text: CAG to PAC: report, scrutiny and action taken Trace an audit observation into constitutional laying, committee scrutiny and documented executive follow-up.

records.title: RTI: first appeal, second appeal and the separate complaint route
records.text: RTI: first appeal, second appeal and the separate complaint route Identify the appellate actor, trigger record, burden and reviewable penalty conditions.

records.title: RPA section 8: offence class, sentence threshold and review
records.text: RPA section 8: offence class, sentence threshold and review Keep conviction, offence-specific thresholds, release and appellate orders distinct.

records.title: Co-operatives in the Constitution: whose rules bind which society
records.text: Co-operatives in the Constitution: whose rules bind which society Decide first whether a society works in one State or many; only then test Part IXB limits on board size, supersession and audit.

records.title: Environmental clearance: category, stages and clocks (EIA Notification 2006)
records.text: Environmental clearance: category, stages and clocks (EIA Notification 2006) Run a project through the EIA Notification: which authority decides, which stages apply, and how long each clock runs.

records.text: Holding H, c and other reserve behaviour fixed, increasing r or e lowers the multiplier. Holding H, r, e fixed, derivative of m with respect to c is (r+e-1)/(c+r+e)^2: negative if r+e<1 and zero if r+e=1. If H changes, model money can rise despite a falling multiplier. This is algebra under assumptions, not a causal forecast. M14 explicit mathematical assumptions/derivation
